options: A centralized system of record that authenticates users and issues the tokens or assertions other applications trust
A backup system used only for storing passwords
A type of antivirus software
A firewall that filters network traffic
questions.explain: An IdP is the authoritative system an organization points everything else at to answer who a user is and whether they're authenticated.

questions.q: Which of the following are real examples of enterprise identity providers named in this lesson?
options: Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
Windows Defender, Norton, and McAfee
Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, and Ping Identity
Chrome, Firefox, and Edge
questions.explain: Entra ID, Okta, and Ping Identity are real, widely used enterprise identity providers.

questions.q: What does the term "identity plane" describe?
options: Identity operating as its own dedicated infrastructure layer that other security controls, like Conditional Access and Zero Trust, depend on
A deprecated term no longer used in security engineering
A single login page with no connection to other controls
A physical server room where identity data is stored
questions.explain: The identity plane is the idea that identity is a layer of infrastructure other controls constantly query and depend on, not just one app among many.

questions.q: In the Conditional Access policy example in this lesson, what does the policy require?
options: Disabling all administrator accounts
MFA for every Global Administrator sign-in, across every connected application
A VPN connection for every user
No authentication at all for administrators
questions.explain: The policy's grantControls require the mfa built-in control for any sign-in matching the Global Administrator role condition.

questions.q: Why is a compromised IdP account especially damaging in an SSO-enabled organization?
options: Because SSO means that one trusted IdP session can reach every connected application
Because SSO only applies to non-administrative accounts
Because SSO has no effect on how many apps a compromised account can reach
Because IdPs cannot be compromised
questions.explain: SSO means every connected app trusts the IdP's decision, so one compromised session at the IdP can reach everything downstream.
